The default for B2B AI companies has become scaling a big forward-deployed engineering team to build custom solutions for each customer. This is especially true for AI companies working with non-technical teams. Even though we work mostly with non-technical teams (customer support teams), Anker and I have chosen not to go that route at Parahelp. Instead, last fall we decided to focus on building infrastructure that enables customer support teams to use AI to easily build their own custom support agent. A big part of our confidence in that decision came from watching non-technical people on our team build with Claude Code. At the time, we had been using Opus 4 in Claude Code for about 2 months, and not only were engineers shipping much more, but non-technical people (like me) were also suddenly shipping UI changes and other product improvements. To this day, Claude Code is a key reason we’ve kept our team so small. ...more

I've always been drawn to what's next. That's one of the reasons I'm so happy to be back at FOSS . Now, 100 days into my role as SVP R&D, one thing stands out: the most important innovations today don't happen within individual technologies and disciplines. They happen at their intersection. The most impactful breakthroughs emerge when hardware, software, biotechnology, data and AI come together to help customers make better decisions and achieve better outcomes. Many people associate FOSS with advanced instruments. And rightly so. But what has surprised me most is how much innovation happens beyond the instruments themselves. One visible example is that half of my R&D colleagues are software developers. That wasn't the case just a few years ago. But innovation is ultimately about more than technology. It takes people with the curiosity to question established ways of thinking, the courage to test new ideas and the persistence to turn possibilities into reality. That mindset is exactly what I encounter every day at FOSS - and what keeps us looking for what's next.

activity.title: Lovable just raised $400M at a $13.3B valuation to build the business that builds businesses. Menlo Ventures came back to lead another round alongside the Scaleup Europe Fund (managed by EQT Group ) as co-lead, who believes what I’ve said from the start: We will build a long-lasting global business from Europe. For me, the most important part of a funding announcement is the accountability that comes with it. At our Series B in December, we committed to deeper integrations, stronger collaboration and governance, and the infrastructure people need to run software at scale. And then we did what we said we would do. Since then, the number of projects built on Lovable went from 25M to 60M, monthly visits to Lovable-built products went from 200M to 900M, and our ARR nearly tripled in these 8 months. This round creates the same kind of accountability. Since we started, Lovable has become the place where founders create million dollar businesses, business leaders spin up new product lines, and people inside companies rewire workflows and build tools that fit their exact needs, typically at a fraction of what software used to cost. There’s a lot more to do. We will create the most intuitive platform to build and run a business. That means: - Understanding what success looks like for you, then helping you achieve it. Not only ensuring your software works but also that you can attract customers, improve workflows, and grow your company. - Deeper integrations that work with your existing tech stack so you can build the interface to your entire business across sales, ops, marketing, finance, etc. - Becoming the safest platform to build and run your business on, which means secured code by default and that you get help to make safe decisions. As you build, the platform carries more of the security weight, spotting risks and helping you close them, so you can move fast without needing to become a security expert. - Staying model-independent and orchestrating the best models for every task so you don’t have to. We’ll continue to absorb the complexity of evaluating and teaching models to route to the best models in the background, to minimize cognitive load for our users. As more people depend on Lovable, the quality standards our team is driving increase every single day. We’re growing the team with people with a founder mindset: curious, ambitious, and who think end to end. Model training, product geniuses, infrastructure tinkerers, and security are the priority. The world is full of ambitious people with deep knowledge of problems worth solving. Very few of them have historically had the power to act on them. Our ambition is to give people that power, and then help them achieve more than they thought possible. Thank you to everyone who has followed along our journey. We have made a lot of progress but we are nowhere close to done, it’s still day zero. See our blog: https://lnkd.in/di5mUqSQ

activity.title: I was the youngest employee at Sana when I joined, at Parahelp I’m the oldest. I just turned 26… There are actually more similarities between the two, then differences - other than the fact that both are Scandinavian. Extreme talent. When I joined Sana, I was so impressed by the team and constantly felt like an imposter. Sana managed to hire some of the most amazing people, including Anton Osika - who unfortunately left before I joined. Parahelp managed to do that too: Mads , Anker and the rest of the team are top notch. The main difference is that we are fully AI enabled at Parahelp, allowing us to do far more with less headcount. Everything is automated and efficient - a truly impressive setup. Customer obsession. I’ve rarely seen companies care as much as they do. At Sana we would call our customers partners, since that’s how we truly viewed them. The Impact (Engagement) team would go above and beyond to make a customer win and pulled out some all nighters once in a while - myself included. In hindsight, our lives would have been significantly easier if we would have used Parahelp from the start. It would have saved us countless of hours… That same care is very visible at Parahelp. No matter if you’re a member of the Customer Acceleration team or not, everyone takes initiatives to respond to our customers within seconds. Even our founders - sometime I think they’re just AI bots given how quick they spot things… Incredible products. I remember the first time I touched Sana. It felt like a magical experience, it made me happy and brought me joy. Same thing with Parahelp. I’m so impressed by the intelligence of our agents and how capable it is. Yesterday I built an entire new integration for a customer with the agent. This would normally have taken me a couple of days, with Parahelp I did it in two hours! I feel extremely lucky to have been part of both! My footprint at Sana was left, now it’s time to do the same at Parahelp. 🚀
